t: That the Act entitled “An Act to permit the American Academy in Rome to enlarge its purposes, and for other purposes”, approved June 6, 1912 (37 Stat. 124), as amended (43 Stat. 635), is hereby amended by striking out “$10,000,000” and inserting in lieu thereof “$25,000,000”.

fable.w: This section only amends an earlier Act by raising a dollar limit for the American Academy in Rome from $10,000,000 to $25,000,000. The tempting reading is that naming a non-federal organization implies outside involvement, but the text provides no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue. No outside party takes part in any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section is a simple amendment to a previous statute, changing a monetary cap from $10,000,000 to $25,000,000. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely a legislative adjustment of funding limits.
qwen_block.s: That the Act entitled “An Act to permit the American Academy in Rome to enlarge its purposes, and for other purposes”, approved June 6, 1912 (37 Stat. 124), as amended (43 Stat. 635), is hereby amended by striking out “$10,000,000” and inserting in lieu thereof “$25,000,000”.

opus.w: The provision only replaces "$10,000,000" with "$25,000,000" in the Academy's 1912 charter act. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. Naming a non-federal organization is not enough: nothing here brings outsiders into a federal decision.
opus.s: is hereby amended by striking out “$10,000,000” and inserting in lieu thereof “$25,000,000”.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a legislative amendment that changes a monetary cap in a previous statute. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties (such as the American Academy in Rome) before the decision is made. The change is enacted directly by Congress without any procedural requirement for outside input.
qwen_chat.s: That the Act entitled “An Act to permit the American Academy in Rome to enlarge its purposes, and for other purposes”, approved June 6, 1912 (37 Stat. 124), as amended (43 Stat. 635), is hereby amended by striking out “$10,000,000” and inserting in lieu thereof “$25,000,000”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the American Academy in Rome is an outside entity and that amending its charter involves some form of consultation or participation. However, the text merely changes a dollar amount in a statute. It does not describe any process of consulting with the Academy, holding a hearing, or seeking input from outside parties before making the decision to change the appropriation limit. The decision is made by Congress through the legislative act itself.
